title: Granadine Confederation
capsule: The Granadine Confederation was a federal republic formed in 1858 when the liberal constitution drafted under President Mariano Ospina Rodríguez replaced the centralist Republic of New Granada with a loose federation of eight sovereign states occupying present-day Colombia and Panama. The confederation's radical federal structure gave each state effective autonomy to legislate independently, including on issues of slavery and individual rights, producing wide legal divergence across the territory. Civil conflict between conservative and liberal factions culminated in the War of 1860–62, which the liberals won under General Tomás Cipriano de Mosquera; the victorious liberals replaced the confederation in 1863 with the United States of Colombia under an even more decentralised constitution.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The confederation's outer boundaries follow well-documented colonial-era jurisdictions inherited from New Granada; internal state boundaries are clearly defined in the 1858 constitution.
